subject: Flapping alerts; missed runs counted one run per firing and calendar-aware
brief:
Improve cronlite's run-log alerts: detect jobs that keep switching between success and failure, and make missed-run detection stricter and aware of blackout calendars.

1. Add `RunLog.transitions(job, last=None)`: how many times the outcome changed between consecutive runs of the job (a success followed by a failure or the other way round), counting only its latest `last` runs when `last` is given; a job without runs has none. A `last` below 1 raises CronError. It also takes `since`, a datetime: when given, only runs that started at or after it are looked at (and `last` then picks the latest of those). `RunLog.stats(job)` also reports this count for all the job's runs, under the key `transitions`.
2. Add `flapping(log, job, window=6, threshold=3)` to the alerts module and export it from the package: an Alert of kind `flapping` when the outcome changed at least `threshold` times within the job's latest `window` runs, otherwise None. It takes the same optional `since` as `transitions`. Its detail reads "<changes> changes in the last <runs> runs", where <runs> is the number of runs actually looked at (fewer than `window` when the job has fewer runs, or fewer since `since`). A window below 2 or a threshold below 1 raises CronError.
3. `missed` gets stricter: one run accounts for one firing only. Firings are matched in time order, and each run serves the earliest firing it can (it must start at the firing time or up to `tolerance` after it); a run already used cannot serve a later firing, so with firings close together a single run no longer hides the ones after it. A run starting before a firing still does not count for it. A negative `tolerance` raises CronError.
4. `missed` takes a new optional `calendar` (a BlackoutCalendar): firings on closed days are never reported as missed.
5. `check` takes three new optional arguments: `flap_threshold` (None by default, which means flapping is not checked at all), `flap_window` (default 6), and `calendars`, a dict from job name to that job's calendar for the missed-run check. Alerts stay ordered by job name and then by kind, now failing, flapping, missed, slow; a job can get both a failing and a flapping alert. Flapping in `check` is judged only on the runs that started at or after the check's `start`, so old unstable runs before the checked period do not raise it. A calendar stored under the key "*" applies to every job that has no entry of its own (a job's own entry wins, even when it closes nothing); without either, a job has no closed days.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
